pages.quiz:
COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.

2. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

3. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Input Cable Tester
   D. International Cricket Team

4. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

5. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.

6. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

7. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Keyboard
   C. Monitor
   D. Speaker

8. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Remove all guards
   D. Work alone with eyes closed

9. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.

10. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

11. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.

12. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Implementation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Relational Database Fundamentals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Structured Query Language and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.

2. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

3. A — Information and Communication Technology

4. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

5. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.

6. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

7. A — CPU

8. B — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

9. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

10. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

11. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.

12. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Object Oriented Programming Concepts; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Object Oriented Programming Implementation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Relational Database Fundamentals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Structured Query Language; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
